The highlighted tokens are typically the word or short phrase that immediately follows the ordinal “first” (or a close equivalent such as “initial,” “second,” “front,” “1st/2nd,” or “depth-first”), completing a “first ___” construction. In other words, the activation is on the noun, verb, or modifier being presented as the first item in an ordering or sequence. A few examples are noisy (code, math, non-English characters), but the dominant pattern is the token that comes right after an ordinal/“first”-like word.
